```{r}
#| include: false
# library(): loads a package so its functions can be used in this session.
# normalizePath(): resolves a path into a canonical absolute path.
# getwd(): returns the current working-directory path.
# file.exists(): checks whether each specified file path exists.
# file.path(): joins path components with the platform-appropriate separator.
# dirname(): returns the directory portion of a file path.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
library(knitr)
project <- normalizePath(getwd())
while (!file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")) && dirname(project) != project) project <- dirname(project)
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(project, "20261.Rproj")))
```
## 1–2. Restaurant conditioning

```{r}
# read.csv(): reads a comma-separated file into a data frame; its first row supplies column names by default.
# file.path(): joins path components with the platform-appropriate separator.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# sum(): adds vector entries; on logical values it counts TRUE entries.
# mean(): computes an average; logical TRUE/FALSE values contribute 1/0, giving a proportion.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# names(): reads or assigns names to vector elements or table columns.
# unname(): removes names or dimension names without changing the underlying values.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
r <- read.csv(file.path(project, "data/module02/restaurant_ratings.csv"))
A <- r$quality_rating == "Very Good"
B <- r$meal_price_usd >= 20 & r$meal_price_usd < 30
ans <- c(A_given_B=sum(A&B)/sum(B), B_given_A=sum(A&B)/sum(A), Joint=mean(A&B), Product=mean(A)*mean(B))
kable(data.frame(Quantity=names(ans),Value=unname(ans)),digits=6)
stopifnot(sum(A&B)==64, sum(B)==118, sum(A)==150)
```

The conditional probabilities are 0.542373 and 0.426667, compared with joint probability 0.213333. The independence product is 0.196667, so independence fails within the finite selection experiment. This arithmetic comparison is not a population hypothesis test. Very Good and Excellent cannot both describe one selected record; both have positive probability, so their zero joint probability cannot equal the product of their marginal probabilities.

## 3. Two selections

```{r}
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
kable(data.frame(Mechanism=c("Without replacement","Independent with replacement"),
                 Probability=c((150/300)*(149/299), (150/300)^2)),digits=6)
```

Without replacement: about 0.249164. With replacement: 0.25. Given a first Very Good selection, the second-selection numerator is 149 and denominator is 299.

## 4. Supplier evidence

```{r}
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# sum(): adds vector entries; on logical values it counts TRUE entries.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# abs(): returns absolute values; a small tolerance in an equality check permits floating-point rounding.
prior <- c(.65,.35); bad <- c(.02,.05)
joint_bad <- prior*bad
posterior_bad <- joint_bad/sum(joint_bad)
joint_good <- prior*(1-bad)
posterior_good <- joint_good/sum(joint_good)
kable(data.frame(Supplier=1:2,Joint_bad=joint_bad,Given_bad=posterior_bad,Given_good=posterior_good),digits=6)
stopifnot(abs(sum(joint_bad)-.0305)<1e-12,abs(sum(posterior_bad)-1)<1e-12)
```

$P(S_1\mid D)=0.426230$, $P(S_2\mid D)=0.573770$, and $P(S_2\mid G)=0.342960$. The 0.05 input is $P(D\mid S_2)$, not the reverse conditional. Individual inspection records and sample sizes behind those stated rates are unavailable; do not fabricate them or claim present-day supplier validation.
